name: Bhai Sati Das
role: Companion of Guru Tegh Bahadur; the Guru's cook and, in some accounts, scribe
summary: Bhai Sati Das (died 1675), younger brother of Bhai Mati Das, served Guru Tegh Bahadur and, Sikh tradition says, was executed in Delhi in November 1675 for refusing to give up his faith.
about: Bhai Sati Das was born in Karyala in the Jhelum region, now in Pakistan, the younger brother of Bhai Mati Das and son of Hira Nand, a follower of Guru Hargobind. According to the Bhatt records he worked in the Guru's kitchen, and some sources say he taught Persian to the young Gobind Rai. He went with Guru Tegh Bahadur to Assam and on the eastern tours, and was there when Chakk Nanaki was founded. In 1675 he was arrested with the Guru near Ropar and taken to Delhi. Sikh tradition says he was executed at Chandni Chowk, tied and wrapped in cotton and set alight, while he kept repeating Waheguru.
kidSummary: Bhai Sati Das was a quiet, hard-working helper of Guru Tegh Bahadur. He helped in the Guru's kitchen and travelled with him. When he was asked to give up his beliefs, he stayed calm and kept saying Waheguru.

story.title: Brothers in service
story.text: Sati Das grew up in Karyala with his older brother Mati Das. Their father had served Guru Hargobind, so both boys learned to serve the Gurus.

story.title: Helping in the kitchen
story.text: Sati Das helped Guru Tegh Bahadur in the Guru's kitchen, and some accounts say he taught Persian to young Gobind Rai.

story.title: Journeys far away
story.text: He travelled with the Guru to Assam and other places in the east, and he was there when the new town of Chakk Nanaki was begun.

story.title: Arrest in 1675
story.text: In July 1675 the Guru set out for Delhi with Sati Das, his brother and Bhai Dayala. They were arrested near Ropar and taken to Delhi.

story.title: Staying steadfast
story.text: Sikh tradition says he was tested in front of the Guru and would not give up his faith, even under great pressure.

story.title: A calm voice
story.text: At Chandni Chowk, Sikh accounts say, he kept chanting Waheguru to the end. A museum there now remembers him and his brother.

teaches: Humble work in the kitchen is real service
Stay calm and kind even in fear
festivals: Martyrdom remembrance of Guru Tegh Bahadur

facts.text: According to the Bhatt Vahi Talauda he served Guru Tegh Bahadur as his cook, and SikhNet calls him a devoted volunteer in the Guru's langar, the free community kitchen.
Some sources say he taught Persian to the young Gobind Rai, who later became Guru Gobind Singh.
Guru Gobind Singh later wrote the Zafarnama in Persian, in 111 verses. If the tradition of Sati Das's Persian lessons is right, he taught the language of that letter, though no source ties the two.

Before his turn he folded his hands, asked the Guru's blessing and said he was glad to be a martyr. The Guru praised his devotion, urged him to accept God's will cheerfully and said his sacrifice would be remembered.
He was tied to a pole, wrapped in cotton fibre and set alight; accounts say he stayed calm and kept repeating the Waheguru mantra.
The Mughal kotwali where he and his companions died was knocked down by the British after the 1857 uprising, and the land then passed to the Sikhs.
He was the last of the three companions to be put to death. The Guru was beheaded early the next morning by an executioner from Samana named Jalal-ud-din.
On the Guru's eastern tours Sati Das and Mati Das were arrested at Saifabad and Dhamtan. Wikipedia says this may have been due to the influence of Dhir Mal, the ulema or orthodox Brahmins.
SikhNet gives his life as 1620 to 1675, and says he was tested and humiliated in front of the Guru but would not give up his faith.
SikhNet's article shows three hukamnamas, letters from the Guru, which it says are held by Sati Das's descendants.
Wikipedia says he had a strong command of Persian, the court language of the Mughal empire.

quiz.q: How were Bhai Sati Das and Bhai Mati Das related?
quiz.why: Sati Das was the younger brother of Mati Das.

quiz.q: Which job did he do for Guru Tegh Bahadur?
quiz.why: The Bhatt Vahi records say he served as the Guru's cook.

quiz.q: Which language do some sources say he taught young Gobind Rai?
quiz.why: Some sources say he taught Persian to young Gobind Rai.

quiz.q: Which mantra did he keep repeating?
quiz.why: Sikh accounts say he kept repeating Waheguru.
